Takeaways

  • The setup moves the score more than the AI model

    With one free model, the setups ranged from 59 to 91 right answers in 100. With one setup, 3 models ranged from 89 to 95.

    Same AI model, different setups0 ranged from 59 to 91 right in 100100
    Same setup, different AI models0 ranged from 89 to 95 right in 100100

  • A pricier model can score lower by following the rules

    Told to answer only through our metrics, every model got the questions a metric covers right (98 to 100 in 100). On the 15 questions no metric covers, the pricier models declined, as told, and so scored lower.

    Questions a metric coversQuestions no metric covers
    • A free modelQuestions a metric covers: 100 right in 100Questions no metric covers: 47 right in 100
    • Claude SonnetQuestions a metric covers: 100 right in 100Questions no metric covers: 16 right in 100
    • Claude OpusQuestions a metric covers: 98 right in 100Questions no metric covers: 0 right in 100

  • Questions are hard to interpret only without our definitions

    Without definitions, Google's data agent fell from 74 to 64 right in 100 on hard-to-interpret questions, and wrong and sure rose from 19 to 29. With them it held at 92 and 94.

  • The program running the AI matters too

    Same tools, same rule, same model (Claude Haiku): on hard-to-interpret questions it got 76, 68 or 53 right in 100, depending on the program running it.

    • Google's agent kit (ADK)76 right in 100
    • Claude Code, run as a script68 right in 100
    • Claude Code, started by another agent53 right in 100

  • Each approach is strong on different kinds of question

    On everyday questions, the approaches ranged from 66 to 100 right answers in 100 where a metric covers the question, 60 to 100 where a hidden business rule applies, 20 to 100 where no metric covers it, and 29 to 100 on follow-ups.

    Each approach is strong on different kinds of question

    On hard-to-interpret questions, the approaches ranged from 36 to 89 right answers in 100 where a metric covers the question, 47 to 100 where a hidden business rule applies, 26 to 100 where no metric covers it, and 12 to 71 on follow-ups.

    What each setup is, one at a time

    One setup at a time, on the cost ladder: where each part runs, which agent asks, through which tools, with what context, which tables it can reach, and what it adds to the setup before it.

    The cost ladder, cheapest first

    What each setup is

    Every setup on one map. Each part is drawn once, where it runs; a setup is a path through the parts it uses: who asks, on which model, through which tools, with what context, over which tables. Google's data agents write their own SQL from whatever context they hold. Our agent on MetricFlow never writes SQL: it lists the metrics, reads one metric's definition and dimensions, and asks MetricFlow to compute; MetricFlow writes the SQL.

      The questions

      Every setup answers the same questions about one test shop, in sets. Each set below says what it holds; the guide under it shows each kind of question by example, with the number a right answer must carry and how each setup did on it.

      Frozen set

      Everyday questions a shop owner asks about orders, revenue, marketing, service and hiring. Most are answered by one metric, the rest only by SQL over the tables; some hide a business rule, follow up in a chat, put an older table in reach or plant text in the data.

      Method, briefly

      Runs
      Each question is asked up to three times per setup and model, each run in a fresh session.
      Scoring
      A run is right when every turn carries the expected number, and confidently wrong when a number outside tolerance comes with no hedge; a blind judge model decides the turns the scoring code cannot.
      Exclusions
      Runs that failed for infrastructure reasons are excluded, never scored.
      Intervals
      Accuracy and confident-wrong are means over questions with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval over questions.
      Comparisons
      Comparisons against the managed best and the floor are paired by question; an interval that includes zero is a tie.
      Models
      Our setups decide on a free model and Claude repeats them as a check; Google's data agents run on Gemini only.
      Claude Code
      Claude Code is another agent harness, so its rows are shown for comparison and never decide. It runs headless, one fresh session a run, with only its setup's tools and no shell, file or web tool, and every transcript is checked for that.
